lean.statement: theorem exists_flat_truncation_tower {C : Type u} [Category.{u} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C} {R : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{u}} (G : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj R)) ℤ) : ∃ (E : ℕ → CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj R)) ℤ) (t : ∀ n : ℕ, E n ⟶ E (n + 1)) (q : ∀ n : ℕ, E n ⟶ G.truncLE (n : ℤ)), (∀ n : ℕ, ∃ b : ℤ, ∀ i : ℤ, b < i → IsZero ((E n).X i)) ∧ (∀ (n : ℕ) (i : ℤ), SheafOfModules.IsFlat ((E n).X i)) ∧ (∀ n : ℕ, QuasiIso (q n)) ∧ (∀ (n : ℕ) (i : ℤ), Epi ((q n).f i)) ∧ (∀ n : ℕ, t n ≫ q (n + 1) ≫ G.ιTruncLE ((n + 1 : ℕ) : ℤ) = q n ≫ G.ιTruncLE (n : ℤ))

statement: Let $(C,J)$ be a small site and $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings. For every cochain complex $G$ of $R$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], there exist complexes $E_n$, maps $t_n:E_n\to E_{n+1}$, and termwise epimorphic quasi-isomorphisms $q_n:E_n\to\tau_{\le n}G$ [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules], for all $n\in\mathbf N$, such that every $E_n$ is bounded above, every term $E_n^i$ is flat [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], and $t_n q_{n+1}\iota_{n+1}=q_n\iota_n$ as maps into $G$, where $\iota_n:\tau_{\le n}G\to G$ is the good truncation inclusion. Bounded above means that for each $n$ some integer $b_n$ has $E_n^i=0$ for $i>b_n$.

proof.text: By Mathlib, G.truncLE 0 has zero terms above zero. Regard it as an object of the full subcategory used by [lem-pc-kflat-bounded-flat-replacement], with bound zero. Its replacement Q.obj F and augmentation epsilon.app F form the initial state: bounded above at zero, flat in every degree, a quasi-isomorphism, and epic in every degree. Also apply this same functor at bound zero to the complex concentrated in degree zero with term M. Its degree-zero augmentation followed by the canonical degree-zero identification is an epimorphism from a flat module sheaf to M, giving the flat-cover hypothesis used by the successor lemma.

A stage n is a dependent pair of a complex E and augmentation q to G.truncLE n, together with the four properties above. Given such a stage, apply [lem-pc-flat-truncation-successor] to obtain a next stage and a transition with the exact compatibility into G. Package the next stage as a subtype witness. Its transition is retained by the existential witness property.

Use Nat.rec starting at the initial stage, choosing the next stage from the one-step existence theorem at every successor. The successor equation of this recursion is definitional. Rewrite by it to get a transition from each stage n to stage n+1, and choose that transition. Project the complexes and augmentations from the stage states. Their subtype properties prove boundedness, flatness, quasi-isomorphy, and termwise epimorphy, and the transition witness property proves strict compatibility. All choice occurs inside the proof of an existential theorem; no definition of module data is introduced.
